# ipzilon_ip_address (Resource)

Occupies a specific IP address in a subnet. Destroy releases it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Occupy a specific free IP address within a subnet.
# status accepts "used" (default) or "reserved"; destroying the resource
# releases the address.
resource "ipzilon_ip_address" "gateway" {
  subnet_id   = ipzilon_next_subnet.example.id
  address     = "10.0.1.10"
  status      = "reserved"
  hostname    = "gw-web-tier"
  description = "Web Tier Gateway"
}

# Available attributes after apply:
# ipzilon_ip_address.gateway.address           → "10.0.1.10"
# ipzilon_ip_address.gateway.hostname          → "gw-web-tier"
# ipzilon_ip_address.gateway.status            → "reserved"
# ipzilon_ip_address.gateway.is_azure_reserved → false
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address` (String) IP address to occupy (e.g. 10.0.1.5). Must be inside the subnet and not already in use.
- `subnet_id` (Number) Subnet containing this IP.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description.
- `hostname` (String) Hostname for this IP — use as the semantic name for the address.
- `status` (String) IP status: used (default) or reserved. To free the address, destroy the resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) IPzilon record ID of the occupied address.
- `is_azure_reserved` (Boolean) True for IPs automatically reserved by Azure (.1 gateway, .2/.3 DNS, broadcast).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Only occupied, reserved or annotated addresses have an ID and can be imported.
terraform import ipzilon_ip_address.example 5
```
